title: Mexico’s Pemex Cuts Debt by More Than US$20 Billion and Raises Refining 81% Compared to 2018, Carpio Says
author: Fernanda Monroy
content:
_This article by[Fernanda
Monroy](https://contralinea.com.mx/author/fermonroy/) originally appeared in
the [October 21, 2026 edition of
Contralínea](https://contralinea.com.mx/interno/semana/pemex-reduce-deuda-en-
mas-de-20-mil-mdd-y-eleva-refinacion-81-frente-a-2018-carpio/), a Mexican
investigative journalism magazine._

Petróleos Mexicanos (Pemex) **reduced its debt** by more than **US$20 billion
in less than two years** and reached its lowest level since 2014, reported its
director general, **Juan Carlos Carpio Fragoso**. He also reported an **81
percent increase in oil refining** compared to 2018 and **production of 1.76
million barrels per day.**

During the morning press conference this Wednesday, October 21, the official
highlighted that the public company's strategy focuses on **maintaining
hydrocarbon production** , **increasing the transformation of oil into fuels**
, **strengthening petrochemicals and fertilizers, and allocating greater
resources to productive projects.**

He indicated that **natural gas production increased 7.5 percent** compared to
2024, to exceed 4.9 billion cubic feet per day. Regarding crude processing, he
said Pemex went from around 612,000 barrels per day in 2018 to **more than 1.1
million barrels currently**. He attributed this growth to the **operation of
the refineries** , the addition of the **Olmeca refinery** , and **operational
improvements at strategic facilities in Tula.**

This progress was also reflected in fuel manufacturing, as the **production of
gasoline, diesel, and jet fuel increased 186 percent** compared to 2018, going
from 350,000 barrels per day to one million.

Carpio Fragoso explained that, of the fuels marketed by the oil company, the
proportion coming from its own facilities went from **24 of every 100 liters
sold in 2018 to 87 of every 100 liters today.** According to the executive,
this change makes it possible to generate greater value within the national
production chain and reduce dependence on external purchases.

In the **petrochemical sector, the production of ethylene derivatives grew 27
percent** compared to 2025, which represents greater availability of domestic
raw materials for industry.

Meanwhile, **fertilizer production increased 16 percent** , with a **36
percent increase** in urea production, in addition to advances in phosphate
and nitrogen inputs for the agricultural sector.

The head of Pemex also reported that **gasoline and diesel sales grew 17.9
percent** **between January and September 2026** , compared to the same period
of the previous year.

On the financial front, he maintained that the **debt reduction** will make it
possible to lower interest payments and **free up resources** to invest in
extraction, refining, and petrochemicals. As part of its growth plans, the
company plans to allocate **more than 1.8 trillion pesos between 2025 and
2030** , coming exclusively from its own resources, to strengthen its value
chain.

In the social sphere, the official detailed that, **between 2025 and September
2026, Pemex allocated almost 6.6 billion pesos to support communities and
strategic regions** where it has operations. These funds were channeled to
roads, infrastructure, health and education works, productive projects, and
community programs.

Finally, he stated that the results are part of a **strategy to strengthen
Pemex** as a public company fundamental to national development, through
greater energy generation and continued investment in the different stages of
the hydrocarbon chain.
